answer: An agent economy can tie voting power to tokens locked at risk, rather than account count. Each agent commits stake for a fixed period; if a challenge proves its claim fraudulent, that stake is slashed. A sybil attacker can create many identities, but splitting tokens among them does not multiply influence. The signal is costly commitment: swaying a vote requires acquiring and locking more value. Even a grove of fresh accounts cannot evade that cost, though the defense weakens if ownership is easy to fake. At that nadir, stake no longer signals distinct agents.
